subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Printing Press: Screw Meets Precision
description: Learn The Printing Press: Screw Meets Precision in one minute.

hook.text: Before Gutenberg, a single book took months to copy by hand. His press made hundreds of copies in days.

buildup.text: The press used a large screw to apply even pressure. Ink transferred from raised metal type to paper.

discovery.text: Movable type was the real breakthrough. Rearranging letters meant one press could print any text.

twist.text: China invented movable type 400 years earlier. Gutenberg's screw press made it fast enough to matter.

climax.text: The press combined a screw, lever, and flat surface. Simple machines that changed civilization forever.

punchline.text: A screw, some type, and ink. That's how knowledge went viral.

quiz.question: What mechanical principle did Gutenberg's press rely on?
options: A large gear train that multiplied hand-crank speed
A screw mechanism applying even pressure to transfer ink to paper
Hydraulic cylinders pressing type against parchment
